{{2010–11 Horizon League men's basketball standings}}
The '''2010–11 Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball team''' represented [[Cleveland State University]] in the [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Their head coach was [[Gary Waters]]. The Vikings played their home games at the [[Wolstein Center]] and are members of the [[Horizon League]]. It was the 80th season of Cleveland State basketball. They finished the season 27–9, 13–5 in Horizon League play to share the regular season conference title with [[2010–11 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] and [[2010–11 Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball team|Milwaukee]]. They lost in the semifinals of the [[2011 Horizon League men's basketball tournament]] to Butler. They were invited to the [[2011 National Invitation Tournament]] where they defeated [[2010–11 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]] before falling to the [[2010–11 College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball team|College of Charleston]] in the second round.

==Preseason==
The preseason Horizon League Coaches' Poll picked the Vikings to finish third.<ref name="horizonleague3">{{cite press release|url=http://horizonleague.org/blog/butler-unanimous-favorite-mack-chosen-player-of-the-year-in-mens-basketball-preseason-poll.html?page=3&sport_id=2&types[]=2|title=Butler Unanimous Favorite, Mack Chosen Player of the Year in Men's Basketball Preseason Poll|publisher=Horizon League|accessdate=2010-12-04|date=2010-10-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110102184409/http://horizonleague.org/blog/butler-unanimous-favorite-mack-chosen-player-of-the-year-in-mens-basketball-preseason-poll.html?page=3&sport_id=2&types%5B%5D=2|archive-date=2011-01-02|url-status=dead}}</ref> Norris Cole was named to the preseason all-Horizon League 1st team.<ref name="horizonleague3"/>

==Regular season==
On November 29, 2010 Cleveland State received their first point in the AP Top 25 poll for the season, that had them 41st.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings/_/year/2011/week/4/seasontype/2|title=2011 NCAA Men's Basketball Rankings - Week 4 (Dec. 5)|publisher=ESPN|access-date=2010-11-29|date=2010-12-04}}</ref> The lone point came from Steve Deshazo of [[The Free Lance-Star]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://hosted.ap.org/dynamic/external/onlinenews.ap.org/top25_basketball/men/index.php?SITE=AP&name=DESHAZO|title=News from the Associated Press; Steve Deshazo Frlnce Star, FdrksbrgVA|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=2010-12-04|date=2010-11-29}}</ref> The game time of the February 5 game against Butler was changed from 2:00 p.m. to 12:00 p.m. to accommodate a broadcast on ESPN2. The attendance at the Butler @ Cleveland State game on February 5 was 8,490. That is the 6th largest home attendance ever for a Cleveland State basketball game.
